TaskDescription:
The two experiment paradigms were designed to quantitatively acquire data related to the different limbs MI tasks.  
The experimental tasks comprised three tasks: left hand-grasping, right hand-grasping and foot-hooking.  
In particular, foot-hooking refers to keeping the heel of the foot stationary while slowly lifting the toe, creating a 45-degree angle with the ground.  
When  the experiment began, visual and auditory instructions are appeared simultaneously.  
The visual cues of MI tasks are provided on the monitor by displaying a brief video on a white background, while resting cue are provided on the monitor by displaying  a white cross sign on a black background.
